name: Lugaro cell (cerebellum)
anatomy_mentioned: just beneath / at the top of the granule cell layer, under the Purkinje cell layer
somata much less numerous than Golgi cells
axons form a parasagittal plexus with long transverse branches parallel to parallel fibers (partly myelinated)
somatodendritic arbors aligned with aldolase C (zebrin II) cerebellar compartments
nt_type: GABAergic/glycinergic (mixed in ~two-thirds of labeled cells; remainder GABAergic-only); classified as an inhibitory Purkinje-layer interneuron (PLI)
morphology_summary: Small, morphologically distinctive inhibitory interneuron of the cerebellar cortex sitting just beneath/within the Purkinje cell layer at the granule cell layer border. Classic form is a slender bipolar cell whose dendrites run parallel to the Purkinje cell layer. Axons form a parasagittal plexus plus long transverse branches (partly myelinated) that run parallel to the parallel fibers; ascending and transverse axons project into the molecular layer. Neighboring cells are interconnected by adherens junctions forming a somatodendritic meshwork beneath the Purkinje cell layer. Hard to distinguish from small Golgi cells by morphology alone under dense labeling.
ephys_summary: Selectively excited by serotonin (5-HT), driven into sustained steady firing in the ~5-15 Hz range; this monoaminergic excitation relays serotonergic signal into the local inhibitory network. Receives monosynaptic inhibitory input from Purkinje cell axon collaterals. As an interneuron-selective interneuron it inhibits Golgi cells and molecular layer interneurons (basket/stellate) but not Purkinje cells, producing disinhibition of both Purkinje-cell and granule-cell pathways. A single Lugaro cell can contact >100 Golgi cells; ~10 Lugaro/globular cells converge onto one Golgi cell.
subtypes_noted: Two related anatomical/molecular variants within the Lugaro/globular class: (1) fusiform Lugaro cells - the classic elongated fusiform soma within the granule cell layer with bipolar dendrites; putative transcriptomic markers Htr2a or Edil3; (2) globular cells - small, rounder/globular soma located directly beneath the Purkinje cell layer; putative markers Aldh1a3 or Slc6a5; silent at rest, driven to spike by serotonin OR noradrenaline (fusiform Lugaro cells respond to serotonin but not noradrenaline), receive strong Purkinje-cell monosynaptic inhibition and likely direct mossy-fiber excitation. Reviews treat these as closely related subgroups of one Lugaro/globular class rather than fully unrelated interneurons. Molecularly distinct from Golgi, candelabrum, and lower molecular layer interneurons.
